title: Treasury Laws Amendment (2019 Measures No. 1) Bill 2019
short_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (2019 Measures No. 1) Bill 2019

speeches.speaker: Stuart Robert
speeches.brief: This bill extends concessional draught beer excise rates to kegs of eight litres or more to support craft beer brewers.

speeches.speaker: Anthony Albanese
speeches.brief: The Customs Tariff Amendment (Craft Beer) Bill 2019 extends concessional excise rates to brewers supplying draft beer in containers of eight litres or more, and increases the maximum annual tax rebate from $30,000 to $100,000. The speaker criticised the government for initially bundling the bill with unrelated superannuation legislation, but welcomed its separation, and noted the craft brewing sector's 547 independent breweries, 4,000 jobs, and $518 million value in 2018.

speeches.speaker: Matt Thistlethwaite
speeches.brief: Labor supported the bills extending concessional excise rates to domestic craft brewers supplying draught beer in kegs of eight litres or more, but opposed schedule 1, which would increase the maximum number of members in self‑managed superannuation funds from four to six, calling it an unrelated and unnecessary addition.

speeches.speaker: Rebekha Sharkie
speeches.brief: The Treasury Laws Amendment (2019 Measures No. 1) Bill 2019 levels the excise playing field so craft brewers no longer pay a higher rate on smaller kegs, a change the member for Mayo had persistently advocated for.

speeches.speaker: Scott Buchholz
speeches.brief: The government will support craft brewers through Schedule 2 and the Excise Tariff Amendment, extend the G20 Global Infrastructure Hub income exemption for four years, and make minor Treasury amendments, while removing Schedule 1—which would have raised the maximum self-managed super fund members from four to six—due to opposition blocking, with plans to revisit it later.
